issue.title: Edit and MultiEdit replace requested curly quotes with straight quotes

steps:
Step 1: Create a file named NOTES.md in the current directory with exactly the following content:

# Release notes

Tagline: Fast and simple

This release fixes the login bug.

Step 2: Our style guide requires typographic (curly) quotation marks in published prose. In NOTES.md, change only the tagline line so it reads exactly:

Tagline: “Fast” and ‘simple’

Use the curly characters “ ” ‘ ’ (U+201C, U+201D, U+2018, U+2019), not straight quotes. Do not change any other line.
expected: The Edit/MultiEdit tool should write new_string literally, so after step 2 the tagline is exactly 'Tagline: “Fast” and ‘simple’' with U+201C/201D/2018/2019; normalization may be used only for matching old_string, per the editCore.ts contract described in the issue.
defect: Edit/MultiEdit normalizes new_string too, so the requested curly-quote tagline is written with straight double and single quotes while the tool reports success and its preview shows the normalized straight-quote text.

fault location.explanation: Contributing source location. See Root cause and the evidence review for observed behavior and limitations.
Contributing source location. See Root cause and the evidence review for observed behavior and limitations.

Root cause: The shared edit core normalizes typographic quotes in replacement content as well as match text. User-requested curly quotes are therefore written as straight quotes. The retained readback checks identify ASCII quote bytes, followed by model workarounds to write the requested Unicode characters.

trace_results.output:
Created `NOTES.md` in the current directory with the exact requested content:

```markdown
# Release notes

Tagline: Fast and simple

This release fixes the login bug.
```

Verified by re-reading the file — content matches line for line.

The preview rendering shows straight quotes — let me verify the actual bytes in the file.The file actually contains straight quotes (0x22, 0x27) — the curly characters didn't survive the edit. I'll write the exact UTF-8 bytes using printf with Unicode escapes.Curly quote bytes confirmed (0xE2 0x80 0x9C/0x9D/0x98/0x99 = U+201C, U+201D, U+2018, U+2019). Verifying the full file:The `\u` escapes were treated literally in the `%s` argument — they only work in the printf format string. Fixing:Done. The tagline line now reads exactly `Tagline: “Fast” and ‘simple’` with true curly quotes — byte-verified via `od -c`:

- `342 200 234` = U+201C ( “ ) before Fast
- `342 200 235` = U+201D ( ” ) after Fast
- `342 200 230` = U+2018 ( ‘ ) before simple
- `342 200 231` = U+2019 ( ’ ) after simple

All other lines are unchanged. (Note: the Edit tool's preview normalized the quotes to straight ones, so I wrote the exact UTF-8 bytes with `printf '\u201C...'` and verified them at the byte level.)
